concept.title: Refactoring Tools
concept.shortdesc: DITA Craft rewrites every reference to an ID, key, or moved file across your whole workspace — including conkeyref matches, which are now verified against the key space before they are touched.

section.title: Overview
section.p: DITA content grows fragile as it grows large: a single renamed ID or moved file can silently break dozens of conref, keyref, and conkeyref pointers elsewhere in the workspace. DITA Craft's refactoring tools rewrite the reference graph for you, so structural edits stay safe even in large, multi-map projects.

section.title: Rename ID or Key
section.p: Place the cursor on an id attribute value, or on a single key name inside a keys="..." attribute, and press F2 (or right-click and choose Rename Symbol). DITA Craft updates every matching href, conref, keyref, and conkeyref across the workspace in one atomic edit.

You can also start from a reference: F2 on the key of a keyref or conkeyref renames that key at its definition (the map that defines it for this topic, key scopes included); on the topic or element part of an href/conref fragment (other.dita#topic/element), or on the element after a key (key/element), it renames that id in the file it is in. Renaming a topic id also updates the topic part of #topic/element references. When the definition cannot be found — a key that is not defined, an element that does not exist — the reason is shown at the cursor instead. A file path is not renamed this way: move the file instead.

Renaming a key now verifies every candidate conkeyref match against the key space before rewriting it — a match on element-ID text alone is no longer enough. A reference that looks like it points at the renamed key but cannot be proven to resolve there is left untouched and logged instead of silently rewritten, eliminating false-positive rewrites in workspaces that reuse the same ID or key name in more than one scope.
section.note: Press Shift+Enter instead of Enter in the rename box to preview every file that will change before anything is written.

section.title: Move Topic with Reference Updates
section.p: Move or rename a .dita, .ditamap, or .bookmap file the normal VS Code way — drag it in the Explorer, or use F2 on the file itself — and DITA Craft keeps every relative reference pointing where it did: each href, conref and conrefend that pointed at the file's old path, in every file across the workspace, and the moved file's own references (links, images, reused content) when it lands in another folder. Files moved together keep pointing at each other. References in comments and CDATA sections, fragment-only references (#topic/element) and web addresses are left as written.

Moving or renaming a whole folder works the same way: everything in it moves — topics, maps, images — so references into the folder from elsewhere follow it, the references its topics make to files outside it are rewritten, and references between its own files stay as they are. Renaming or moving any other file your topics and maps refer to — an image, a .ditaval in a <ditavalref>, a PDF — updates the references to it as well. The settings that name a file or folder follow it too: the root map (ditacraft.rootMap), the templates folder (ditacraft.templatesPath), the XML catalog (ditacraft.xmlCatalogPath), the preview's custom CSS (ditacraft.previewCustomCss), the custom rules file (ditacraft.customRulesFile) and the DITAVAL filter of your publishing profiles — in the workspace or user settings, written the way they were (relative, ${workspaceFolder}/… or absolute) — and so does the active preview filter.
The updates are made and saved right after the move, and a notification says how many files were updated.

section.title: Extract Topic from Section
section.p: Select — or simply place the cursor inside — a <section> in the active topic and run DITA: Extract Topic from Section. DITA Craft:

ol.li: Creates a new standalone topic file from the section's content.

Matches the new file's root element to the source topic's type — a <concept> section produces a new <concept>, a <reference> section produces a new <reference>, and anything else falls back to a generic <topic>.
Replaces the original section with an <xref> pointing at the new topic.

section.note: A <taskbody> does not allow <section> as a child at all — DITA tasks use <context>, <steps>, and <result> instead. Running this command inside a task topic is blocked with a clear message rather than producing structurally invalid content.

section.title: Inline Conref
section.p: The reverse of content reuse: place the cursor on (or inside) an element that carries a conref or conkeyref attribute and run DITA: Inline Conref. DITA Craft resolves the reference and writes the element as DITA resolves it: the target element's content, the element's own attributes, and the target's attributes it does not set (a reused <note type="important"> stays important; an attribute set to -dita-use-conref-target takes the target's value). Relative references — on the element and inside its content: links, images, nested reuse — are rewritten for the topic's folder, so they still point where they did. The reference attributes are removed, and the target's id and any nested descendant id values are left out, so the result never introduces a duplicate-ID violation. A conrefend range or a conaction push is not one element and is not inlined.

The edit applies immediately to the active file, without a workspace-wide preview — unlike Find & Replace or Batch Metadata Update, this is a single, cursor-scoped change. Undo with Ctrl+Z if you change your mind.
